output:
The feature: Lift CRUD backend
Three files, wired as server.js → liftRoutes.js → liftController.js → Lift.js → MongoDB:

Lift.js — the data shape
A Mongoose schema defining what a 'lift' document looks like in MongoDB:

liftCode, block, unit — required strings, liftCode must be unique.
type — must be one of Passenger/Freight/Mixed.
status — one of Active/Maintenance/Out of Service/Decommissioned, defaults to Active.
capacity — required number, min 1.
manufacturer, installDate, lastServiced — optional metadata.
timestamps: true auto-adds createdAt/updatedAt.
Straightforward and fine as-is.

liftController.js — the business logic
Six handlers, each wrapped in asyncHandler (so thrown errors get forwarded to Express's error middleware instead of crashing the process):

listLifts — supports filtering by ?status=, ?type=, and a free-text ?q= search across liftCode/block/unit/manufacturer (built as a regex, with special chars escaped — good practice).
liftStats — runs 5 counts in parallel via Promise.all for a dashboard-style summary.
getLift / createLift / updateLift / deleteLift — standard CRUD, using ApiError.notFound/badRequest for consistent error responses and an ok() helper for consistent success responses.
The pattern (asyncHandler + ApiError + ok()) is a clean, common Express convention.

liftRoutes.js — the endpoints
Maps HTTP verbs to controller functions under /api/lifts, and gates the router behind requireAuth, with write operations (POST/PUT/DELETE) further gated behind requireRole('Admin','Manager').

What's actually broken
The logic above is sound in concept, but none of it can run right now. I checked the rest of the repo:

Wrong require paths — liftController.js does require('../models/Lift'), but the file actually lives at models/lifts/Lift.js. Same problem in liftRoutes.js: require('../controllers/liftController') should be ../controllers/lifts/liftController.
utils/ApiError, utils/asyncHandler, utils/apiResponse don't exist anywhere in the repo. There's no src/utils/ folder at all.
middleware/auth (requireAuth, requireRole) doesn't exist either — there's no src/middleware/ folder, and no auth library (jsonwebtoken, bcrypt, etc.) even in package.json. There's no login/JWT system anywhere yet.
The routes are never mounted. server.js:21-26 still has /api/lifts as a commented-out TODO, despite the commit message claiming it was 'mounted in server.js.'
The only existing route (uploads.js) uses plain try/catch + res.json/res.status directly — it doesn't follow the asyncHandler/ApiError/ok() convention your new controller assumes, so that convention is being introduced but its supporting files were never created.
Net effect: if you mounted this router right now, require() would throw immediately on server start (module not found), before a single request could even reach it.

To fix, in order
Fix the two require paths (../models/lifts/Lift, ../controllers/lifts/liftController).
Either build src/utils/asyncHandler.js, ApiError.js, apiResponse.js — or drop that pattern and rewrite the controller with plain try/catch like uploads.js does.
Decide on an auth strategy (JWT is the common fit here) and build src/middleware/auth.js, or strip requireAuth/requireRole from the routes until auth exists.
Uncomment/add the app.use('/api/lifts', require('./routes/lifts/liftRoutes')) line in server.js.
Want me to go ahead and build the missing pieces (utils + a basic JWT auth middleware) and wire it up, or would you rather do that part yourself now that you know what's missing?
action-detail:
All fixed and verified. Here's what changed:

Fixed require paths

liftController.js — now points at ../../models/lifts/Lift and ../../utils/* (was ../models/Lift, ../utils/*).
liftRoutes.js — now points at ../../controllers/lifts/liftController (was ../controllers/liftController).
Created the missing utils (the convention your controller assumed but that didn't exist yet):

ApiError.js — error class with .badRequest/.unauthorized/.forbidden/.notFound helpers, each carrying a statusCode.
asyncHandler.js — wraps async handlers so thrown/rejected errors get forwarded to Express's error middleware.
apiResponse.js — ok(res, data, message, statusCode) for a consistent success envelope.
Stripped auth from liftRoutes.js per your call — removed requireAuth/requireRole, left a TODO comment to re-add them once a login system issuing role-bearing JWTs exists.

Mounted the router and added error handling in server.js:

app.use('/api/lifts', liftRoutes) — actually wired now (previously just a commented-out TODO despite the commit message).
Added a catch-all error-handling middleware at the end of the middleware chain — without this, anything thrown via ApiError/asyncHandler would have no handler to catch it and the request would hang instead of returning a JSON error.
Verified: installed npm install in backend/ (node_modules was missing), then required all three lift modules directly — they load without errors — and syntax-checked server.js. I did not start the server against a live Mongo connection since I don't have your DATABASE_URL; once your .env is filled in, npm run dev should bring /api/lifts up live.

One thing worth flagging: /api/lifts write endpoints (POST/PUT/DELETE) are now open with no auth at all — fine for local dev, but don't ship that to anything public-facing before the auth system lands.
